input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The shape check before Editor.edit_files tests only for os.PathLike and no longer wraps a plain str, so a string filename is passed on as an iterable and consumed character by character when building the editor command.
- failure path: click.edit(filename="notes.txt") launches the editor with the nine single-character files n, o, t, e, s, ., t, x, t instead of notes.txt; saving creates stray files in the working directory and the intended file is never opened.

Reviewer finding
- description: The check was changed from `isinstance(filename, str)` to `isinstance(filename, os.PathLike)`, so plain string filenames are no longer wrapped in a tuple. A `str` is not an `os.PathLike`.
- rationale: Trigger: `click.edit(filename="foo.txt")`, the most common usage. The string is passed to `edit_files` as an iterable of characters, so the editor is launched with one argument per character (`f`, `o`, `o`, ...) instead of the single file. The user sees the wrong files being opened, or an error. It should check `isinstance(filename, (str, os.PathLike))`.
critique: The finding pins down the same mechanism. The check now tests only for os.PathLike, so a plain str is not wrapped and gets iterated character by character into editor arguments. It also gives the same trigger, click.edit with a string filename.
